part.text:
The user wants a new Maven Java project that parses and generates JSON. Let me set up the project structure. I'll use Jackson for JSON processing since it's the most common library.

Let me create:
- pom.xml
- src/main/java/... 
- src/test/java/...
- .gitignore

Let me pick a groupId/artifactId. Something like `com.example` / `json-app`.

Java 26 is available, but Maven compiler with release 26? Let me set release to 21 for stability... Actually Java 26 is installed. Maven 3.10.0 supports it. But compiler plugin needs to support. Let me use a reasonable release like 21. Actually, to avoid issues, use 17 or 21. I'll use 21.

Let me create the project. I'll use Jackson databind.

Let me create a simple app that parses and generates JSON. I'll make a model class and a main.

Let me create the todo list? This is a multi-step task. Let me just do it.

Structure:
```
/work
├── pom.xml
├── .gitignore
└── src
    ├── main/java/com/example/jsonapp
    │   ├── Main.java
    │   └── model/Person.java
    └── test/java/com/example/jsonapp
        └── JsonRoundTripTest.java
```

Let me check latest Jackson version. Jackson 2.18.x or 2.17.x. I'll use 2.18.2. Actually let me keep it safe and recent. I could check but no internet necessarily. Let me use 2.17.2 which is widely available. Hmm, I want the build to succeed. Let me create and run mvn to verify.

Let me use Jackson 2.18.2. If it fails downloading, I'll adjust. Let me just try.

Actually, let me consider using the dependency-reduced approach with jackson-databind.

Let me write the files.

For the model, using a Java record would be idiomatic and modern. Jackson supports records. Let me use records. With release 21.

pom.xml:
- junit-jupiter for tests
- maven-compiler-plugin release 21
- exec-maven-plugin maybe not necessary

Let me write.
I'll scaffold a Maven project using Jackson for JSON handling.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>json-app</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>json-app</name>
    <description>Maven Java project for parsing and generating JSON</description>

    <properties>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
        <jackson.version>2.18.2</jackson.version>
        <junit.version>5.11.4</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.fasterxml.jackson.core</groupId>
            <artifactId>jackson-databind</artifactId>
            <version>${jackson.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.fasterxml.jackson.datatype</groupId>
            <artifactId>jackson-datatype-jsr310</artifactId>
            <version>${jackson.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.13.0</version>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.2</version>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
                <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.0</version>
                <configuration>
                    <mainClass>com.example.jsonapp.Main</mainClass>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

part.text:
Everything works. But note createdAt serialized as numeric timestamp rather than ISO string. That's because JavaTimeModule by default writes as timestamps unless WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS is disabled. Let me fix that to make it idiomatic (ISO-8601). Add `.disable(SerializationFeature.WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS)`. Actually that's an often-desired behavior. Let me improve.

The round trip still works. I'll make it output ISO date strings, which is more standard for JSON.
The dates serialize as numeric timestamps; let me make them ISO-8601 strings, which is the common JSON convention.

part.text:
Done. Maven project set up with Jackson, verified with tests and a runnable demo.

- `pom.xml` — Java 21, Jackson databind + JSR-310, JUnit 5
- `src/main/java/com/example/jsonapp/Main.java` — parse/generate demo
- `JsonMapperFactory.java:12` — shared `ObjectMapper` with ISO-8601 dates
- `model/Person.java` — record mapped to JSON
- `JsonRoundTripTest.java` — round-trip test

Run with `mvn test` or `mvn exec:java`.
